claim: resolve_task_type() — the real production entry point used by terminal_client.py, routes_echo_studio.py, and run.py's mirror_echo() — only calls detect_task_type() (where the classifier lives) when compute_intent_heatmap()'s own top-category score is below 0.4; otherwise the heatmap's own primary category is used directly and the classifier is never consulted.
result: def resolve_task_type(prompt): heatmap = compute_intent_heatmap(prompt); primary = max(heatmap, key=heatmap.get); if heatmap[primary] < 0.4: primary = detect_task_type(prompt); return primary, heatmap
limitations: none — direct source read of unmodified, non-forbidden-target file

claim: The real, currently-trained classifier — exercised through the real, unmodified resolve_task_type() production function via an availability-flag ablation, never mutated — genuinely overrides the keyword-only routing decision on constructed inputs that push compute_intent_heatmap()'s confidence below 0.4.
command_or_test: 6 constructed multi-category-keyword-collision prompts; for each, compared resolve_task_type(p) [classifier live] against resolve_task_type(p) with app.core.echo_model_orchestrator.TASK_TYPE_CLASSIFIER_AVAILABLE monkeypatched False for the duration of that one call only [classifier ablated], same real persisted model both times, read-only predict() only
result: 4/6 prompts triggered the <0.4 fallback branch (classifier actually consultable); of those, 2/6 (33% of triggered cases) showed the real classifier output changing resolve_task_type()'s final routing decision relative to the classifier-ablated counterfactual (both flipped coding→creative on high classifier confidence 0.944-0.975)
limitations: constructed adversarial inputs, not organic production traffic; first probe attempt (mission32_probe.py) used the wrong counterfactual (detect_task_type() keyword ladder instead of the classifier-ablated full pipeline) and produced a false override signal on 2 prompts where the classifier was never even consulted (heatmap confidence already >=0.4) — caught and corrected before being reported as a finding, see Adversarial Findings section
